The closest matches are papers on LLM-driven style change and personalization, not on synthetic data curation specifically. One paper finds that LLM rewriting normalizes personal narratives, reducing first-person pronouns and contractions while increasing vocabulary diversity and word length [1]. Another shows that post-editing LLM-generated drafts can move text toward a writer’s personal style, but the result still retains detectable LLM traces [3]. A broader study of human and LLM writing also finds that model and genre shape style more than prompting or decoding strategy [5].

If you mean methods for making synthetic text more like a target author, the benchmark paper on personalization says such methods modulate style but do not bridge the gap to human authorship [9], and a federated approach aims to preserve author-specific signals instead of homogenizing them [10].
